In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no clear indications for a change in blocking in the Northern Hemisphere.
the synoptic blocking index of Tibaldi and Molteni (1990) is a useful tool to detect blocking situations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that blocking events are associated with a significant increase in the occurrence of extreme precipitation and drought events.
the 2009/10 and 2011/12 winter seasons were characterized by an anomalous blocking activity over the North Atlantic and the Eurasian continent, respectively.
the blocking detection based on geopotential height anomalies has a good performance, but it can be improved by using the geostrophic winds instead, which are less affected by the orography.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the blocking index proposed in Molteni and Tibaldi (1994) and used in many studies (e.g., Scaife et al., 2010; Sun et al., 2009) can be misleading when it comes to detecting the large-scale blocking structures.
the blocking detection method has to be tailored to the specific application and that the blocking index should not be used in isolation.
the Tibaldi-Mol-teni blocking index can be used to detect blocking events in a reliable and objective way.
